title: Assessment of pre‐release mating levels during the production of Thaumatotibia leucotreta (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae) in a sterile insect technique programme
content:
Pre-release mating assessments across different production and release stages of Thaumatotibia leucotreta in a sterile insect technique programme.


Abstract

Thaumatotibia leucotreta is endemic to sub-Saharan Africa and is a key citrus pest of phytosanitary importance to certain export markets. To manage this pest, a systems approach that may include the sterile insect technique (SIT) has been deployed. SIT involves mass-rearing the target insect, sterilising insects using ionising radiation, and releasing them into the field to suppress wild populations. This study investigated pre-release mating levels during the production and release stages of a T. leucotreta SIT programme over the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 seasons. Sampling occurred at three stages: moth eclosion, post-irradiation, and field release across different regions. Females (n = 400 per stage) were randomly collected from 20 different cardboard collection boxes and immediately frozen to prevent spermatophore degradation. Subsequent laboratory dissections of the moth's bursa copulatrix under a stereomicroscope quantified the number of mated females and spermatophore abundance. The results demonstrated significant variation in the 2024/2025 season, with more mating incidences and spermatophore transfers occurring during eclosion, post-irradiation, and the Sundays River Valley release stage relative to the Olifants River Valley. Conversely, these metrics did not differ significantly from one another during the 2025/2026 season, marking a significant inter-seasonal decline in pre-release mating relative to the 2024/2025 season. Pre-release mating of sterile insects reduces insects' mating vigour, and curtailing these sterile-to-sterile matings is highly desirable because it ensures sterile individuals target their wild counterparts. Consequently, these data provide a vital baseline for optimising the efficacy and execution of the SIT programme as a sustainable management strategy for T. leucotreta in South Africa.
